comment: The register of which repos are frozen and why. Kept here, in MAM-basics, rather than as a marker file inside each frozen repo: writing such a marker would itself change the repo and destroy the very last-changed date the freeze exists to preserve. Deliberately separate from in/vendoring_policy.json, whose per-repo 'ignore' flag means 'do not scan this repo for vendoring' -- a different question from 'do not touch this repo at all'. The lists are not the same one: CCAR-Psalms is frozen here and is not ignored there, so neither may be derived from the other.
location_comment: Ben's decision, 2026-08-31: C:\Users\BenDe\FrozenRepos is NOT part of the expected machine layout, and no machine is to be made to have one. It was a transitional hedge -- an almost-trash staging area created on 2026-08-07, when moving the six frozen clones out of GitRepos felt safer than deleting them, and dropping them from all-repos.code-workspace took that file from 30 folders to 24 -- and the hedge is spent, because all six remotes are ARCHIVED on GitHub and so are read-only and durable. The archived remote is the copy of record; a clone was only ever a second copy of it. A machine with no FrozenRepos directory is conforming, not broken, so do not restore one and do not read its absence as a defect. WHAT ENFORCES THE FREEZE IS ABSENCE FROM A WORKSPACE FILE, NOT LOCATION: every sweep in py/main_repo_util.py iterates the repos a workspace file lists and resolves them under --repos-root, so a repo no workspace file lists cannot be reached by any action -- not just --run-black, which was the only action ever consulting this list (open issue #211). This file therefore no longer skips anything at run time, and that is not a defect either: the register's job is to record WHICH repos are frozen and WHY, which all-repos.code-workspace's silence cannot do. Two consequences of the freeze being structural. (1) A frozen repo is not swept for leftover agent worktrees either, which is fine while nothing runs sessions in a frozen clone, and is the thing to revisit if that ever changes. (2) To thaw a repo: un-archive it on GitHub, since an archived remote refuses a push with 403, then clone it back into GitRepos, re-add it to all-repos.code-workspace, and delete its entry here. HOW THE HEDGE WAS FOUND TO BE SPENT, recorded so that nobody re-diagnoses the missing directory. A sync on 2026-08-31 rebuilt this machine and did not restore FrozenRepos; nothing broke, and a full session's work noticed nothing missing. That sync restored every non-archived repo Ben owns and not one archived repo -- the six repos listed below being both the only archived ones and the only absent ones -- so the sync cannot produce FrozenRepos on any machine. Restoring the directory would be a manual act, repeated per machine, that nothing checks and nothing reminds anyone about. That is why the arrangement is retired: not because the six clones were unwanted, but because it was a fixture no mechanism maintained.

repo_visibility.comment: Which repos are public and which are private, so a maintenance sweep can keep the two apart. Declared here rather than queried from GitHub because the sweeps must work offline and because Gist-ArtScroll is a gist, which `gh repo view` cannot resolve at all. Ben's decision, 2026-08-27: a repo's NAME is not itself private, so naming the private repos in this public file is fine -- what must not cross is their CONTENT, meaning paths inside them, file names of theirs, and findings about them. py/repo_util/report_destination.py is what enforces that, refusing to write a report covering a private repo into a public repo's tracked tree; py/tests/test_repo_visibility_declared.py is what keeps this map complete, failing if all-repos.code-workspace lists a folder no entry here classifies. Verified 2026-08-27 against `gh repo view bdenckla/<name> --json visibility` for the 18 first-class repos and `gh api gists/f04699f2a9c4eccd3220751fdb233722 --jq .public` for Gist-ArtScroll, which was named plain ArtScroll here until 2026-08-31.

Taamey_D.comment: The public face of the private hbofonts repo, added to this map and to all-repos.code-workspace on 2026-08-31. hbofonts/ps1_release_all3.ps1 writes into it by the SIBLING RELATIVE PATH ..\Taamey_D, so the release only works while this clone sits beside hbofonts under GitRepos -- it is a build target, not a dormant 2024 repo, and its own last commit of 2024-01-22 makes it look like one. The release fills three destinations, each wiped with Remove-Item -Recurse -Force first, so docs/ and sources/ are wholly generated and nothing there should be hand-edited: docs/ is the documentation site behind bdenckla.github.io/Taamey_D/, Taamey_D_and_friends.zip is the ttf/woff/woff2 release for Shofar_D, Taamey_B and Taamey_D, and sources/ is a DELIBERATELY REDUCED source set -- only the -nofea.sym.sfd and .sym.fea variants, never the plain .sfd or .fea, which stay private in hbofonts. hbofonts' fourth font, Keter_D, is not released at all.

github-misc.comment: Tracks the canonical copies of the dotfiles, ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md and the hebrew-prose skill among them.

MAM-private.comment: Holds several evacuated private trees, each as a top-level directory rather than a clone of its own, so a finding here names a path two levels deep and is a finding about a tree as much as about this repo. Deliberately not enumerated: the guard needs the visibility, not the inventory, and MAM-private/doc/near-aleppo-privacy.md is the governing statement of what about these trees may reach a public repo. Read it before writing public prose about any of them; its section 4 gives the mechanical backstop grep and the two ways that grep misleads.

CCAR-Psalms.comment: Paused client project. Not among the repos in/vendoring_policy.json ignores, which is why that flag cannot stand in for this list.

MAM-for-CCAR.comment: Paused client project. Note this one was six months rather than years old when frozen, so its last-changed date only starts testifying to the pause from here.

mamgo-auto-edits.comment: Archived on GitHub, so the remote is READ-ONLY and no maintenance commit can ever land: a push returns 403, 'This repository was archived so it is read-only'. Found 2026-08-07 the hard way, by a .gitattributes standardization commit that had to be dropped again because it could not be pushed. Archived-on-GitHub and frozen-here nearly coincide -- the five repos above are all archived too -- but neither list may be derived from the other, and 2026-08-07 showed both edges at once: this repo was archived and not frozen, while breuer-cos was frozen and deliberately NOT archived, so that its issues stay writable.

TMC.comment: Paused project, frozen alongside the MAM-for-* client repos.

gitrepos_setup_rule.comment: The complete definition of which repos belong under C:\Users\BenDe\GitRepos, so that 'set up GitRepos' on a new machine and 'sync GitRepos' on an existing one are the same reproducible question. Written 2026-08-31, after a sync cloned a discontinued repo back onto the disk. Before this, no list on disk matched the disk: all-repos.code-workspace and repo_visibility hold the same 19 repos as each other, while 27 are present, and neither the gists nor the exclusions were derivable from anything. Apply the clauses in order; the result reproduced the 27 repos present on 2026-08-31 exactly.
clauses: 1. START with `gh repo list bdenckla`, keeping only repos that are neither archived nor forks. On 2026-08-31 that was 26 of 48.
2. SUBTRACT every name in repos_to_keep_absent (see that key for why each is listed).

3. SUBTRACT every name in frozen_repos. Ben's decision, 2026-08-31: frozen repos are NOT to be cloned on a fresh machine. State this clause explicitly and do not skip it on the grounds that all six frozen repos happen to be archived on GitHub today, which would make clause 1 appear to cover them. That coincidence is exactly what the mamgo-auto-edits comment in frozen_repos warns against: archived-on-GitHub and frozen-here nearly coincide, but neither list may be derived from the other, so a repo un-archived later would silently start being cloned.
4. ADD the gists listed under `gists` below. Gists are invisible to `gh repo list`, so no enumeration can ever produce them and clause 1 cannot be made to cover them.
5. The number of clones under GitRepos should then equal the number of directories there; anything left over is either a decision nobody recorded or a repo that should be removed.

gists.comment: Cloned like repos but unreachable by `gh repo list`, so their URLs are recorded here or they are unrecoverable. Gist-Hebrew-World is why this key exists: on 2026-08-31 its URL existed nowhere on the machine except inside its own clone's git remote, so deleting that clone would have destroyed the knowledge that it should exist. py/repo_util/repo_selection.py carries a clone URL for Gist-ArtScroll too, for a different purpose -- the message shown when a workspace folder is missing -- and that is not a substitute for this list, since Gist-Hebrew-World is in no workspace file.

repos_to_keep_absent.comment: Repos that must NOT have a clone in C:\Users\BenDe\GitRepos, and why. Ben's decision, 2026-08-31. THIS IS NOT frozen_repos, and neither list may be derived from the other, exactly as the comment at the top of this file says of frozen_repos and in/vendoring_policy.json: a frozen repo's clone is kept, merely left untouched so its last-changed date keeps testifying to the pause, whereas a repo listed here should have no clone on this machine at all. NOTHING READS THIS AT CLONE TIME, and that is not an oversight awaiting a script. There is no sync program on this machine: a 'sync' is a Claude Code session answering a free-text request, which on 2026-08-31 enumerated `gh repo list bdenckla`, diffed the result against `ls` of GitRepos by eye, and typed the missing names into a literal clone loop. So the mechanism that consults this register is the instruction in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md (canonical copy github-misc/dot-claude/CLAUDE.md) telling such a session to read it before cloning anything. If that instruction is ever dropped, this key goes back to being documentation that governs nothing.

trope.comment: Discontinued 2026-03-19 in favour of MAM-basics, per the repo's own README. Ben parked its clone the same day as GitRepos.old/trope.old.use-mam-basics-instead, and on 2026-08-31 a sync session cloned it straight back into GitRepos -- because the March decision was recorded only in that repo's README and in the parked directory's name, and the sync read neither. That is the whole reason this key exists. Both copies were removed 2026-08-31, reclaiming about 1.0 GB (414 MB fresh clone, 598 MB parked copy). The remote is live and complete, so `gh repo clone bdenckla/trope` reconstructs it in full if it is ever wanted.
trope.remote_status: Not archived as of 2026-08-31, and so indistinguishable from a live repo to anything that enumerates GitHub. Its README promises archival 'once all open issues have been closed or copied to other repositories'; there are 111 open issues and 382 closed, which is what still blocks that.
